1	# ROADMAP: engine registration = complete CSR-test gate
2	
3	Goal (user): `andesim` registers a vsim engine, and registration PASSES only
4	after every CSR the engine's config supports is completely tested.
5	
6	## Design principle: measure, don't model
7	
8	The engine is the ground truth for itself. We stop GUESSING which CSRs exist
9	from config knobs or spec conditions -- that mapping lives only in the RTL and
10	is fragile to hand-copy -- and instead ASK the vsim engine directly (a probe).
11	Each source shrinks to its true minimal job:
12	
13	| source | role |
14	|---|---|
15	| **vsim probe** | THE truth: existent CSR set + reset values (measured on the reset hart) |
16	| config.inc | identity only: `sha256` = registration key; + fallback for the un-probeable few |
17	| spec inventory | the map: which addresses to probe, names, DS order, read-side-effect skip-list |
18	| RTL `existent_csr` | optional cross-check for the read-side-effect CSRs the probe must skip |
19	| QEMU | workload payload + independent `--verify` oracle -- NOT existence |
20	
21	Why not config alone: spec speaks architecture (`mmsc_cfg.PMNDS`), config speaks
22	knobs (`NDS_*`), neither holds the bridge. Why not QEMU: it is a different
23	implementation with its own (larger, coarser-than-a-config-hash) CSR set --
24	using its drain to decide vsim transport over-claims and faults the DM sweep.
25	
26	## The invariant the gate enforces
27	
28	For a built engine (identity = engine name + `config.inc` hash), every
29	`implemented` CSR (measured by the probe) must be in exactly one bucket:
30	
31	- **transported + tested** -- restored at resume, drained, `--verify`-compared,
32	  AND has its own per-CSR round-trip test.
33	- **named-excluded** -- not transported, with a named reason
34	  (`EXCL_MODE|RV32|DEBUG|SIDEFX`, `CONST_RO`, `gate=off`, ...).
35	
36	Neither-bucket = silent state loss = FAIL. Transported without its own test = FAIL.
37	
38	Locked definitions:
39	- "supported" = the `implemented` (probe-measured) set, not just transported.
40	- "completely tested" for un-writable control CSRs = read-back round-trip
41	  (read crt0 value -> stash -> re-read in ROI -> `bne` + `--verify`), NOT a
42	  destructive blind write.
43	
44	## Discovery vs verification (only verification runs an ELF)
45	
46	- **Discovery = the probe.** Reset hart, checked `csrr` over the inventory. NO ELF.
47	  Yields: existent set, reset values, over-claim + under-claim checks. One-time,
48	  at registration.
49	- **Verification = the generated fixtures.** Run ELFs to prove each transported
50	  CSR round-trips. After discovery, transported set only.
51	
52	## What already exists (reuse, do not rebuild)
53	
54	- `tests/engines/<engine>-<hash>/csr_manifest.csv` -- the 232-row table.
55	- `tests/engines/gen_manifest.py` -- three-way audit. NOTE: its `implemented`
56	  comes from a hand-traced RTL param dict `P` (line 30) and its reset values
57	  from an ELF-keyed baseline capture (line 119) -- both replaced by F3's probe.
58	- `tests/engines/gen_fixtures.py` + `safe_write_policy.csv` -- write-survival
59	  fixtures for the write-safe subset.
60	- `tests/engines/test_registration_guard.sh` -- presence + hash gate.
61	- `tests/engines/test_registration_fixtures.sh` -- safe-write fixtures pass.
62

68	  failing check. A script reads `csr_manifest.csv` and EXITS NONZERO if any row
69	  is `implemented in {yes,partial}` AND `transported=no` AND its

# ROADMAP: engine registration = complete CSR-test gate

Goal (user): `andesim` registers a vsim engine, and registration PASSES only
after every CSR the engine's config supports is completely tested.

## Design principle: measure, don't model

The engine is the ground truth for itself. We stop GUESSING which CSRs exist
from config knobs or spec conditions -- that mapping lives only in the RTL and
is fragile to hand-copy -- and instead ASK the vsim engine directly (a probe).
Each source shrinks to its true minimal job:

| source | role |
|---|---|
| **vsim probe** | THE truth: existent CSR set + reset values (measured on the reset hart) |
| config.inc | identity only: `sha256` = registration key; + fallback for the un-probeable few |
| spec inventory | the map: which addresses to probe, names, DS order, read-side-effect skip-list |
| RTL `existent_csr` | optional cross-check for the read-side-effect CSRs the probe must skip |
| QEMU | workload payload + independent `--verify` oracle -- NOT existence |

Why not config alone: spec speaks architecture (`mmsc_cfg.PMNDS`), config speaks
knobs (`NDS_*`), neither holds the bridge. Why not QEMU: it is a different
implementation with its own (larger, coarser-than-a-config-hash) CSR set --
using its drain to decide vsim transport over-claims and faults the DM sweep.

## The invariant the gate enforces

For a built engine (identity = engine name + `config.inc` hash), every
`implemented` CSR (measured by the probe) must be in exactly one bucket:

- **transported + tested** -- restored at resume, drained, `--verify`-compared,
  AND has its own per-CSR round-trip test.
- **named-excluded** -- not transported, with a named reason
  (`EXCL_MODE|RV32|DEBUG|SIDEFX`, `CONST_RO`, `gate=off`, ...).

Neither-bucket = silent state loss = FAIL. Transported without its own test = FAIL.

Locked definitions:
- "supported" = the `implemented` (probe-measured) set, not just transported.
- "completely tested" for un-writable control CSRs = read-back round-trip
  (read crt0 value -> stash -> re-read in ROI -> `bne` + `--verify`), NOT a
  destructive blind write.

## Discovery vs verification (only verification runs an ELF)

- **Discovery = the probe.** Reset hart, checked `csrr` over the inventory. NO ELF.
  Yields: existent set, reset values, over-claim + under-claim checks. One-time,
  at registration.
- **Verification = the generated fixtures.** Run ELFs to prove each transported
  CSR round-trips. After discovery, transported set only.

## What already exists (reuse, do not rebuild)

- `tests/engines/<engine>-<hash>/csr_manifest.csv` -- the 232-row table.
- `tests/engines/gen_manifest.py` -- three-way audit. NOTE: its `implemented`
  comes from a hand-traced RTL param dict `P` (line 30) and its reset values
  from an ELF-keyed baseline capture (line 119) -- both replaced by F3's probe.
- `tests/engines/gen_fixtures.py` + `safe_write_policy.csv` -- write-survival
  fixtures for the write-safe subset.
- `tests/engines/test_registration_guard.sh` -- presence + hash gate.
- `tests/engines/test_registration_fixtures.sh` -- safe-write fixtures pass.

  `test_registration_completeness.sh`. Real manifests clean (140 implemented
  rows); injected under-claim caught; both engines pass. Turn the printed under-claim report into a
  failing check. A script reads `csr_manifest.csv` and EXITS NONZERO if any row
  is `implemented in {yes,partial}` AND `transported=no` AND its
  `gate_or_disposition` is not a named `EXCL_*` / `gate=off` reason.
  RED: a fixture manifest with one deliberate under-claim -> script fails;
  a clean manifest -> passes.
  Key files: `tests/engines/check_completeness.py` (new),
  `tests/engines/test_registration_completeness.sh` (new, glob-picked by
  `test_all.sh`), `tests/engines/README.md`. Deps: none (pure andesim).

  Original plan below:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Andes-CSR capability parity (the flywheel / drift guard).
#
# The offline deriver (scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py) computes, from a
# core's config.inc, which Andes CSRs it implements. The vsim
# engine compiles the SAME gate logic (src/hybrid/andes_caps*.hpp) and reports
# the list at runtime via `--describe` ("andes_csrs"). Fed the engine's OWN
# embedded build config.inc, the two must be byte-identical -- a disagreement
# means the resume/drain capability gate is wrong for that engine.
#
# Runs against EVERY built engine under $VSIM_BIN_DIR (each sim_* binary with
# a V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc beside it) -- a single hardcoded engine left
# new engines with zero parity coverage. Uses the engine's build config.inc
# (the exact blob the binary embeds), so offline and online share one source.
# The --describe half is opportunistic: it needs the engine rebuilt with the
# S3 describe change (a prebuilt binary that omits "andes_csrs" is skipped).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

DERIVE="$ROOT/scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py"
[ -f "$DERIVE" ] || fail "missing deriver: $DERIVE"

VSIM_BIN_DIR="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/../vsim_andesim/build}"

checked=0
for ENG in "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_*; do
  [ -x "$ENG" ] || continue
  name=$(basename "$ENG")            # sim_<engine>
  engine=${name#sim_}
  # The engine's embedded config.inc (copied next to its Verilated objects).
  CFG="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V$engine/obj_sc/config.inc"
  [ -f "$CFG" ] || fail "$name present but its build config.inc not found at $CFG"

  offline=$(python3 "$DERIVE" "$CFG") || fail "deriver failed on $CFG"
  [ -n "$offline" ] || fail "deriver produced an empty list for $CFG"

  online=$("$ENG" --describe 2>/dev/null \
    | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(" ".join(json.load(sys.stdin).get("andes_csrs", [])))' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$online" ]; then
    echo "[skip] $name --describe has no andes_csrs (rebuild vsim with the S3 change)"
    continue
  fi

  [ "$online" = "$offline" ] || fail \
    "PARITY MISMATCH ($engine): --describe andes_csrs != offline deriver"$'\n'"  describe: $online"$'\n'"  offline:  $offline"
  echo "[ok] $engine: --describe == offline deriver"
  checked=$((checked + 1))
done

[ "$checked" -gt 0 ] || { echo "[skip] no built engines under $VSIM_BIN_DIR"; ok "andes caps parity (skipped)"; exit 0; }
ok "flywheel: --describe == offline deriver on $checked engine(s)"

2	//
3	// A core implements an Andes custom CSR only when the matching feature is
4	// configured into it (config.inc). Restoring a CSR the target core lacks can
5	// hang the DMI handshake -- observed on ax45mpv_premium for ucode (no DSP) and
6	// mecc_code (no ECC). So the resume/drain loops transport only the CSRs the
7	// target core supports, decided here from the core's feature gates.
8	//
9	// This header is Verilator/SystemC-free: it maps a CSR address to its gate and
10	// answers "does a core with these gates support this CSR". The binding of each
11	// gate to the core's compiled-in `_NDS_*` config macros lives in the sim binary
12	// (see andes_caps_from_config), so this stays unit-testable in isolation.
13	#ifndef ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
14	#define ANDES_HYBRID_ANDES_CAPS_HPP
15	
16	#include <cstdint>
17	#include <string>
18	#include <vector>
19	
20	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
21

24	// The hardware feature that gates each transported CSR. ALWAYS = unconditionally
25	// present (a base machine CSR every core has; never gated off). The first block
26	// gates the v3 Andes custom CSRs; the second block (UMODE..TRIGGER) gates the v4
27	// M-ext CSRs (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST) -- standard + Andes M-mode CSRs whose
28	// existence depends on a privilege level or extension the core may not have.
29	enum class AndesGate : uint8_t {
30	  ALWAYS = 0,
31	  DSP,
32	  CODENSE,
33	  ZCMT,        // standard Zcmt table jump (jvt); NOT implied by CoDense
34	  POWERBRAKE,
35	  STACKSAFE,
36	  ECC,
37	  PMA,
38	  ILM,
39	  DLM,
40	  PERF_MONITOR,
41	  // The Andes PMNDS counter scheme (SPA: mmsc_cfg.PMNDS). RTL ground truth
42	  // (kv_csr_dec.v existent_csr): these CSRs exist iff PERFORMANCE_MONITOR
43	  // AND NOT SSCOFPMF -- a core with the standard Sscofpmf count-overflow
44	  // extension REPLACES the Andes scheme. The _UMODE/_SMODE variants add the
45	  // privilege term the spec conditions carry (PMNDS & misa[20] / misa[18]).
46	  PMNDS,        // Andes-scheme perf counters (perf monitor && !Sscofpmf)
47	  PMNDS_UMODE,  // PMNDS && U-mode
48	  PMNDS_SMODE,  // PMNDS && S-mode
49	  ALT_FP,       // umisc_ctl: spec ALT_FP_FMT|CST_CTL, RTL BF16_ARITH|ACE
50	  // v4 M-ext gates.
51	  UMODE,       // needs U-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 2)
52	  SMODE,       // needs S-mode  (NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS == 3)
53	  EPMP,        // ePMP / Smepmp (mseccfg)
54	  SMRNMI,      // resumable NMI (mnscratch/mnepc/mncause/mnstatus/mnvec/mrnxvec)
55	  EXCSLVL,     // exception save levels (msave*)
56	  CLIC,        // CLIC / enhanced CLIC (mtvt/mintthresh/mcirq_entry)
57	  SMSTATEEN,   // state-enable (mstateen0..3)
58	  CCTL,        // cache control CSRs (mcctlbeginaddr/mcctldata)
59	  PPI,         // private peripheral interface base (mppib)
60	  FIO,         // fast IO base (mfiob)
61	  TRIGGER,     // debug triggers (tselect/tdata1/tdata2/tcontrol/mcontext)
62	};

64	// Map an Andes CSR (by address) to the feature gate that enables it. Addresses
65	// are the HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST scalars plus the PMA block. A CSR with no
66	// custom-extension gate is ALWAYS (a base machine CSR every Andes core has).
67	// Maintainer note: a CSR added to HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST that needs gating must
68	// get a case here, else it defaults to ALWAYS (transported unconditionally).
69	constexpr AndesGate andes_gate_for(uint16_t csr_addr)
70	{

72	    case 0x801: return AndesGate::DSP;           // ucode (DSP overflow flag)
73	    case 0x800: return AndesGate::CODENSE;        // uitb  (CoDense table base)
74	    // jvt is Zcmt's table-jump base, NOT part of classic CoDense (exec.it +
75	    // uitb): a CoDense core without Zcmt faults a csrr of it (seen on
76	    // ax45mpv_premium, where it aborted the drain CSR sweep).
77	    case 0x017: return AndesGate::ZCMT;           // jvt   (Zcmt only)
78	    case 0x7C5: return AndesGate::POWERBRAKE;     // mpft_ctl
79	    case 0x7C2: return AndesGate::ECC;            // mecc_code
80	    case 0x7C6:                                   // mhsp_ctl
81	    case 0x7C7:                                   // msp_bound
82	    case 0x7C8: return AndesGate::STACKSAFE;      // msp_base
83	    case 0x7C0: return AndesGate::ILM;            // milmb (ILM base)
84	    case 0x7C1: return AndesGate::DLM;            // mdlmb (DLM base)
85	    // v4 M-ext CSR gates (HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST).
86	    // The PMNDS counter block (SPA existence: mmsc_cfg.PMNDS, plus misa[20]
87	    // or misa[18] for the U/S members). Over-claiming any of these faults a
88	    // PB csrr with cmderr=3, aborting a CSR sweep -- seen live for 0x7D1 on
89	    // premium (M-only) and 0x7CF on advanced (Sscofpmf replaces PMNDS).
90	    case 0x7CF: return AndesGate::PMNDS;          // mcounterinten
91	    case 0x7CE: case 0x7D1: case 0x7D3:           // mcounterwen, mcountermask_m/_u
92	      return AndesGate::PMNDS_UMODE;
93	    case 0x7D2: return AndesGate::PMNDS_SMODE;    // mcountermask_s
94	    case 0x30A: case 0x306:                       // menvcfg, mcounteren
95	    case 0x808: case 0x80B: case 0x811:           // uzobctl, ucctlbeginaddr, sleepvalue
96	      return AndesGate::UMODE;
97	    // umisc_ctl: "Access Mode: User and above" is WHO may touch it, not an
98	    // existence condition -- spec existence is ALT_FP_FMT | CST_CTL (RTL:
99	    // BFLOAT16_ARITH | ACE, no privilege term). The UMODE gate under-claimed
100	    // it on both (M-only) engines; found by the registration audit.
101	    case 0x813: return AndesGate::ALT_FP;
102	    case 0x7D5: return AndesGate::SMODE;          // mslideleg
103	    case 0x747: return AndesGate::EPMP;           // mseccfg
104	    // The STANDARD counters exist under either perf-monitor scheme (Zihpm);
105	    // only the Andes PMNDS block above is scheme-dependent.
106	    case 0x320: case 0xB03: case 0xB04: case 0xB05: case 0xB06:  // mcountinhibit, mhpmcounter3-6
107	    case 0x323: case 0x324: case 0x325: case 0x326:              // mhpmevent3-6
108	      return AndesGate::PERF_MONITOR;
109	    case 0x740: case 0x741: case 0x742: case 0x744:  // mnscratch, mnepc, mncause, mnstatus
110	    case 0x7DE:                                       // mrnxvec
111	      return AndesGate::SMRNMI;
112	    // mnvec is base Andes NMI state -- spec "IM Requirement: Required", RTL
113	    // decodes it unconditionally on cores that lack Smrnmi entirely. It was
114	    // wrongly grouped with the Smrnmi CSRs and under-claimed on every engine.
115	    case 0x7C3:                                   // mnvec
116	    case 0x7C9: return AndesGate::ALWAYS;         // mdcause (base Andes trap CSR)
117	    case 0x7D6: case 0x7D7: case 0x7D8: case 0x7D9:  // msavestatus, msaveepc1, msavecause1, msaveepc2

120	    case 0x307: case 0x347: case 0x7EC:           // mtvt, mintthresh, mcirq_entry

122	    case 0x30C: case 0x30D: case 0x30E: case 0x30F:  // mstateen0..3

124	    case 0x7CB: case 0x7CD: return AndesGate::CCTL;  // mcctlbeginaddr, mcctldata

2	//
3	// run_process spawns a child, captures its stdout, and kills it after a
4	// timeout -- the primitive the engine registry uses to ask `<bin> --describe`
5	// and the plan executor (F6) uses to run orchestrated legs. F5 extends this
6	// file with exec_passthrough (inherit stdio, no timeout) for fast/cycle.

8	#define ANDESIM_PROCESS_HPP
9	
10	#include <functional>
11	#include <string>
12	#include <string_view>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	struct RunResult {
18	  int rc = -1;                // child exit status, or -1 if killed/abnormal
19	  std::string out;            // captured stdout
20	  bool timed_out = false;     // killed because it exceeded the timeout
21	  bool spawn_failed = false;  // pipe/fork failed before the child ran
22	};
23	
24	// Run argv (argv[0] resolved via PATH), capturing stdout. The child's stdin
25	// and stderr are redirected to /dev/null. If the child runs longer than
26	// timeout_ms it is SIGKILLed and timed_out is set.
27	RunResult run_process(const std::vector<std::string>& argv, int timeout_ms);
28	
29	// Run argv to completion with the child INHERITING this process's stdout and
30	// stderr (its output streams straight to the terminal) and stdin from
31	// /dev/null; chdir to `cwd` first if non-empty. No capture, no timeout. Returns
32	// the child's exit code, 128+signal if it was signalled, or -1 on spawn
33	// failure. Used by `build` to delegate to setup.sh / build_*.sh / make.
34	int run_inherit(const std::vector<std::string>& argv, const std::string& cwd);
35	
36	// Run argv to completion with the child INHERITING all three std streams
37	// (stdin, stdout, stderr) -- the transparent-passthrough mechanism behind
38	// `run --mode fast|cycle`: the engine reads/writes the terminal directly,
39	// so an interactive gdbstub or semihosting console works unchanged. No chdir,
40	// no capture, no timeout. Returns the child's exit code, 128+signal if it was
41	// signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.
42	int exec_passthrough(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);
43	
44	// Fork a child that execs argv with inherited stdio and return immediately
45	// without waiting. Used by `run --mode cycle --gdb` to launch vsim in the
46	// background before exec-ing ICEman in the foreground. Returns the child pid
47	// on success, -1 on empty argv or fork failure.
48	int fork_background(const std::vector<std::string>& argv);
49	
50	// Run argv with BOTH stdout and stderr captured (separate pipes) and stdin
51	// inherited, streaming each complete line to `on_line(stream, line)` as it
52	// arrives -- stream is 1 (stdout) or 2 (stderr), line excludes the trailing
53	// newline. The callback owns presentation (it decides what to write to the real
54	// streams), so this is the filtered counterpart to exec_passthrough: same "run
55	// to completion, no timeout, propagate exit code" contract, but the parent sees
56	// every line. A final unterminated line is delivered too. Returns the child's
57	// exit code, 128+signal if signalled, or -1 on spawn failure / empty argv.

# run --verify contract (verify_oracle F4): opt-in oracle cross-check.
#   1. hybrid marker --verify  -> oracle leg + "[verify] PASS", rc 0
#   2. hybrid pc --verify      -> same through the exit_pc oracle path
#   3. default (no --verify)   -> no verify leg, no verify output

set -uo pipefail

ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --verify \
      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker --verify rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[verify\] PASS' || fail "marker: no [verify] PASS: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[state-diff\] PASS' || fail "marker: no state-diff detail: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'window_cycles' || fail "marker: cycle figure missing: $OUT"
ok "hybrid marker --verify: oracle cross-check PASS"

      --pc-start "0x${MARKERS%% *}" --pc-end "0x${MARKERS##* }" --verify \

# Registration guard (tests/engines contract, deliverable 4).
#

# a stale registration (engine rebuilt with a different config) fails loudly
# with "run the bring-up registration". Registrations without a built engine
# are reported but do not fail: "not built" is not "removed" (the engine may
# be built elsewhere; see README.md's deregistration section).
set -uo pipefail

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

  [ -x "$ENG" ] || continue
